note: Likelihoods are expert-written, not learned. Every confirmed fix tunes them later.

hypotheses.name: Thermal fuse
hypotheses.fix: a cheap thermal fuse, about ten dollars, that most people can swap in twenty minutes; a clogged vent usually blew it, so we clean that too

hypotheses.name: Heating element
hypotheses.fix: a new heating element, a bigger part but still doable at home

hypotheses.name: High-limit / cycling thermostat
hypotheses.fix: a small thermostat part, usually an easy swap

hypotheses.name: Timer / control
hypotheses.fix: a timer or control board, best checked by a pro

hypotheses.name: Power (breaker, one 240V leg)
hypotheses.fix: resetting the dryer's breaker, which may fix it for free

tests.label: Breaker
tests.prompt: A half-tripped breaker can cut the heat while the drum still turns, and resetting it is free. Your breaker box is usually a gray metal door in the garage, basement, or a hallway closet. Find the switch labeled dryer, push it fully off, then back on. Does it heat now?

tests.label: Drum
tests.prompt: Start the dryer. Does the drum turn and does the light come on?

tests.label: Warmth
tests.prompt: Think about the last time you ran it: when you opened the door, was there any warmth at all, or was it completely cold?

tests.label: Fuse
tests.prompt: Your meter has a dial and two wires, one red, one black. Turn the dial to the picture that looks like a little sound wave or speaker. Touch the two metal tips together. Do you hear a beep? Good, that means it works. Now, with the dryer unplugged, the fuse is a small white oval piece behind the back panel. Touch one tip to each little metal tab on it. Beep or no beep?

tests.label: Element
tests.prompt: With the dryer still unplugged and the meter on the little sound wave picture, touch one tip to each end of the long metal heating coil, the two metal screws where the wires attach. Beep or no beep?

tests.label: Thermostat
tests.prompt: Still unplugged, with the dial on the little sound wave picture: the thermostat is a small round metal disc near the heater, with two metal tabs. Touch one tip to each tab. Beep or no beep?
